security.notes: The change REMOVES a silent downgrade-to-mock security hazard on authorization, queue, checkpoint, audit, and idempotency persistence paths; fail-closed posture consistent with PRs #247/#249. No new external input surface. Repository state: secret literals remain stripped as of #249 (verified absent from runtime code at this head); rotation runbook still pending owner execution.

changes: getSafeDatabase() now throws SafeSqliteUnavailableError when the better-sqlite3 native binding cannot load; the in-memory mock is reachable ONLY behind allowMockFallback:true or SAFE_SQLITE_ALLOW_MOCK=1 and never when NODE_ENV=production.

Call-site classification fixed: 9 production-critical SQLite stores keep the fail-closed default (SQLiteRenderQueue, CheckpointDB, queue-db, audit-logger, voice-benchmark, DurableAuthorizationStore, ProviderApiOperationJournal, NotebookOperationJournal, EpistemicBudgetReservation); only the degradation-tolerant SceneIntentAnalyzer LLM cache opts into the dev-only mock.
getSqliteHealth() probe added and wired into HealthManager as an explicit sqlite-persistence dependency so missing persistence surfaces in readiness checks instead of being invisible.

Real persistence bug fixed (found by new restart-persistence test): DurableAuthorizationStore.get() omitted the persisted consumed_at column on read-back, so CONSUMED authorization timestamps were lost across restarts.

Regression suites added: missing-binding simulation via in-process .node loader break (proves fail-closed construction/import of production stores, mock unreachable in production, non-durability, env-gate semantics, health probe honesty); real-SQLite restart persistence (queue, authorization CAS state, provider idempotency); source-audit test locking the call-site classification.
